There are two performance obligations, one for the sale of goods and the other for the sale of discount vouchers. Their standalone prices are:

|---|---|

| Total | 20,400 |

For Year 2023 – 2024
The transaction price of ₹ 18,000 is the sale price less the current discount of 10%. It is to be allocated between the performance obligations of goods and discount vouchers proportionately

The transaction price of ₹ 18,000 is to be allocated to goods to be recognised as Revenue in 2023 – 2024: $\text{₹ }18{,}000 \times \frac{\text{₹ }18{,}000}{\text{₹ }20{,}400} = \text{₹ }15{,}882$
The transaction price of ₹ 18,000 is to be allocated to the Discount Voucher to be recognised as a liability: $\text{₹ }18{,}000 \times \frac{\text{₹ }2{,}400}{\text{₹ }20{,}400} = \text{₹ }2{,}118$

For Year 2024 – 2025
In 2024-25, this liability on account of Discount Voucher, recognised in the year 2023 – 2024, will be cancelled and revenue will be recognised for ₹ 2,118 when the discount voucher is redeemed or expires.
The Transaction Price for additional sale is ₹ 14,000 less 50% discount voucher = ₹ 7,000;
Total Revenue recognised for the year 2024 – 2025 is $\text{₹ } 7{,}000 + \text{₹ } 2{,}118 = \text{₹ } 9{,}118$

Computation of Average Past Adjusted Profit before Tax

| Year | Profit (₹) | Weights | Weighted Profit (₹) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 – 2023 | 3,75,200 | 1 | 3,75,200 |
| 2023 – 2024 | 5,15,200 | 2 | 10,30,400 |
| 2024 – 2025 | 6,55,200 | 3 | 19,65,600 |
| Total | | 6 | 33,71,200 |

Average Past Adjusted Profit before Tax $= \frac{\text{₹ }33{,}71{,}200}{6} = 5{,}61{,}866.667$

In this case, using a simple average is not appropriate, as it does not accurately reflect the profit trend. The simple average of past adjusted profits is: $\frac{\text{₹ }3{,}75{,}000+\text{₹ }5{,}15{,}200+\text{₹ }6{,}55{,}200}{3} = \frac{\text{₹ }15{,}45{,}600}{3} = \text{₹ }5{,}15{,}200$. This figure is lower than the third year's profit (₹ 6,55,200) and merely equals the second year's profit (₹ 5,15,200). This undermines the upward trend in profitability.

Since the profit after tax has been increasing steadily by ₹ 70,000 per year, applying a weighted average with weights of 1:2:3 provides a more realistic estimate of the Future Maintainable Profit, which is the relevant figure for goodwill valuation, not merely an average of past profits.

Computation of Goodwill
Computation of Normal Profit
Normal profit $= \text{ Average trading capital employed } \times \text{ Normal rate of return}$
$= \text{₹ } 20{,}34{,}200 \times 10 \% = \text{₹ } 2{,}03{,}420$
Computation of Super Profit
Super profit $= \text{ Future maintainable profit after tax } - \text{ Normal profit}$
$= \text{₹ } 2{,}80{,}933.334 - \text{₹ } 2{,}03{,}420$
$= \text{₹ } 77{,}513.334$
Calculation of Goodwill
Goodwill $= 3 \text{ years' purchase of super profits}$
$= 3 \times \text{₹ } 77{,}513.334 = \text{₹ } 2{,}32{,}540$

Calculation of Capital Employed

| Particulars | (₹ in crores) |
|---|---|
| A) 12% Debt Capital, i.e. Debt | 2,000 |
| B) Equity Share Capital | 500 |
| C) Reserve & Surplus | 7,500 |
| D) Equity (B + C) | 8,000 |
| E) Capital Employed (Debt + Equity) = A + D | 10,000 |

Calculation of Cost of Debt after Tax

| Particulars | Figures |
|---|---|
| A) Cost of Debt in % before Tax | 12.00 |
| B) Tax on Cost of Debt in % $( A \times 0.30 )$ | 3.60 |
| C) Cost of Debt in % | 8.40 |

Calculation of Cost of Equity
According to the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM)
$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Cost of Equity Capital} &= \text{Risk Free Rate} + \text{Beta}(\text{Market Rate} - \text{Risk Free Rate})\\
&= 6\% + 1.50(15\% - 6\%)\\
&= 6\% + (1.50 \times 9\%) = 6\% + 13.50\% = 19.50\%
\end{aligned}
$$

Calculation of Weighted Average Cost of Capital & Cost of Capital Employed

| Particulars | Figure |
|---|---|
| A) % of Debt to Capital Employed $= \text{₹ } 2{,}000 \text{ crores} / \text{₹ } 10{,}000 \text{ crores}$ | 20% |
| B) % of Equity to Capital Employed $= \text{₹ } 8{,}000 \text{ crores} / \text{₹ } 10{,}000 \text{ crores}$ | 80% |
| C) Weighted Average Cost of Debt $= A \times 8.40$ | 1.68% |
| D) Weighted Average Cost of Equity $= B \times 19.50$ | 15.60% |
| E) Weighted Average Cost of Capital $= C + D$ | 17.28% |
| F) Cost of Capital Employed $= \text{₹ } 10{,}000 \text{ crores } \times E$ | ₹ 1,728 crores |

Calculation of Economic Value Added
$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Economic Value Added} &= \text{Net Operating Profit after Tax} - \text{Cost of Capital Employed}\\
&= \text{₹ }2{,}100\text{ crores} - \text{₹ }1{,}728\text{ crores} = \text{₹ }372\text{ crores}
\end{aligned}
$$

Calculation of Market Value Added

- Increase in EVA $= \frac{\text{₹ }372\text{ crores} - \text{₹ }250\text{ crores}}{\text{₹ }250} \times 100 = 48.80\%$
- Likely increase in the share price $= 25 \% \text{ of } \text{₹ } 200 = \text{₹ } 50$
- Share price after increase $= \text{₹ } 200 + \text{₹ } 50 = \text{₹ } 250$
- Total Number of Shares $= \frac{\text{₹ }500\text{ crores}}{\text{₹ }10} = 50\text{ crores}$
- Market Value of Equity $= 50 \text{ crores } \times \text{₹ } 250 = \text{₹ } 12{,}500 \text{ crores}$
- Market Value Added (MVA) $= \text{ Market Value of Equity } - \text{ Book Value of Equity}$
- MVA $= \text{₹ } 12{,}500 \text{ crores } - \text{₹ } 8{,}000 \text{ crores } = \text{₹ } 4{,}500 \text{ crores}$
